title: Floor Apple Silicon top bars to the camera notch cutout
head: 8249e4f87e03
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: New Apple Silicon users never receive the notch-safe layout
leads.consequence: Fresh accounts inherit the stock centerAnchor=omarchy.clock and all five center widgets; the package also seeds a completed marker for every migration in /etc/skel, so this migration does not run for them. With show_notch=1 the bar height is floored but the clock/indicators remain behind the physical cutout. Existing accounts without a user shell.json also hit the migration's -f guard and keep the same shipped layout. Give first run a notch-safe per-screen layout, or ship a hardware-aware default without relying on a one-shot rewrite.
leads.triage: already in Opus F2 (new installs); corroboration

leads.summary: Migration permanently moves a user's center widgets on all outputs and bar orientations
leads.consequence: Hardware detection is the only guard. Even a user-chosen bottom, left or right bar (no top notch floor), replacement bar (bar.id), external monitor, or an Apple machine with show_notch=0 loses its selected centerAnchor and moves every custom center widget to the right on every screen. The root built-in bar only floors top panels, and shell.json is shared between all displays. A test on a bottom bar yielded center=[] and right=[clock,tray]. Gate on a genuinely notched top panel and avoid rewriting the user's global layout; use per-screen draw-time placement instead.
leads.triage: already in Opus F2 (all Apple Silicon, any position); corroboration

leads.summary: A floored top bar is still visible when toggled off
leads.consequence: The bar remains mapped and parks upward by -root.barSize, but its new implicitHeight is max(root.barSize,notchFloor). With the shipped 26px bar and a Pro panel's 32px cutout at scale 2, roughly 6 logical pixels of bar surface remain on-screen when the bar-off flag is set. The exclusion zone is ignored, not the visible pixels or input area. Park by the per-window actual implicitHeight/thickness and add an assertion for that case.

leads.summary: A positive notch-height override bypasses the per-screen notch detection
leads.consequence: On any Apple Silicon host with [bar] notch-height=40, the ternary chooses 40 before calling BarModel.notchHeight. It thus floors every top bar on that host, including DP/HDMI external monitors and the 16:10 non-notched M1 Air, to at least 40 even though the derived geometry would return zero. The global calibration should only replace a positive cutout height on the matching built-in panel, not replace eligibility screening.

leads.summary: The migrated indicators widget becomes zero-width at its new right-hand position when all indicators are inactive
leads.consequence: The stock center includes omarchy.indicators. Migration moves it into right and clears center. With no active indicators, Indicators.implicitWidth is zero until indicatorAreaHovered/centerSectionRevealHeld. Hovering the right-hand zero-width widget cannot itself set indicatorAreaHovered, while centerSectionRevealHeld is set by the now-empty center region's HoverHandler, so a user cannot discover inactive indicators by hovering where the migration moved them. Hovering empty center unexpectedly reveals icons at the right. Preserve a hover target for this widget or adapt reveal to its new location.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up 1 confirmed from source (0 px widget, peek only from empty center, icons next to tray); one sentence published in migration finding

leads.summary: The migration breaks symlinked shell.json dotfiles
leads.consequence: -f follows the user's symlink, jq reads the external canonical config, but mv installs the temporary inode over the link instead of editing its target. Subsequent dotfiles changes no longer apply; the source config stays centered and a later reinstall of the symlink restores the notch overlap. A sandbox fixture recorded symlink=no after a successful exit while the linked original still contained the center clock. Treat a symlink as a supported config shape and preserve its linkage or decline safely.
leads.triage: already in Opus F7 (symlink); dropped from public text after self-check F-5 (common repo pattern)

leads.summary: Migration drops existing shell.json mode and loses atomicity across file systems
leads.consequence: mktemp is not created beside the user config. Replacing shell.json with it changes an existing 0644 file to 0600 in the normal case (sandbox stock mode=600 after 0644 seed); custom permissions/ACLs likewise are not preserved. If TMPDIR and HOME are on different file systems, mv must copy rather than rename, so the watched shell.json can be observed partway through the replacement. Stage in the config directory, preserve intended mode, and write atomically.
leads.triage: 0600 mode part corroborates Opus F7; cross-filesystem atomicity is hypothetical; not published

leads.summary: Reset commands bring back the notch-obscured center layout after migration is marked done
leads.consequence: omarchy bar defaults and omarchy refresh shell repopulate center from unchanged stock shell.json. omarchy reinstall configs copies /etc/skel over the user's config and migration markers. The per-user marker prevents omarchy-migrate from moving the widgets again on later updates. The notch then hides the restored clock and indicators until manually rearranged. Keep a hardware-aware default/reset path or make placement a per-screen runtime behavior.
leads.triage: already in Opus F2 (omarchy bar defaults); corroboration

leads.summary: Open #13362 implements the same notch fix differently and collides with this PR's files and layout semantics
leads.consequence: #13362 is not stacked (read-only compare status diverged) and also adds bin/omarchy-hw-apple-silicon and test/shell.d/bar-notch-test.sh, with different contents. Its bar reads package-described per-panel cutouts, parks the hidden bar by full thickness and only moves center widgets beside right at draw time on that one notched top screen, keeping the configured center on external screens. This PR's one-time global rewrite, if retained, leaves no center entries for #13362 to preserve on external screens. The merged copies of Bar.qml/BarModel.js contain conflict markers, so pick one approach or coordinate files and migration rather than merging both features as written. GitHub reports #13362 MERGEABLE against its current base, not against this PR.
leads.triage: already in Opus F1; coordinator verified #13362 file list via gh

leads.summary: The new notch test passes even when hardware detection is forced on for every machine
leads.consequence: It only checks that the detector is executable, never runs it against a no-device-tree or Apple input, and its migration fixture shadows it with an exit-0 stub. The bar host Process is tested via regex only. In disposable copies, replacing the helper with unconditional exit 0 and independently replacing the QML Process command with echo yes both left the entire new test green under LC_ALL=C. Either mutant can put non-Apple hosts through the migration or notch floor. Add executable detector fixtures with a private device-tree path or injected checker, and exercise the Process output path.
leads.triage: already in Opus F8 (no-apple-gate mutant); corroboration

leads.summary: Malformed but version-accepted center data aborts the remaining migration queue
leads.consequence: For shell.json version=1 with bar.layout.center='clock', jq's length test passes, then string+array in the rewrite raises exit 5. omarchy-migrate runs migrations with bash -euo pipefail and does not touch this marker or start later migrations after failure; every future update retries and blocks at the same point. The shell's normal load accepts any version=1 object and its bar normalization can cope with a malformed layout. Check center's type before mutating, and make invalid data a no-op or give a specific repair diagnostic.
leads.triage: already in Opus F7 edge shapes; public framing narrowed after self-check F-4

leads.summary: User-facing bar docs/template omit the new calibration setting and still describe the migrated center as the default
leads.consequence: [bar] notch-height is the only advertised calibration path for panels that differ from the hardcoded table, but neither the bar settings reference nor the shipped theme template names it. The manual says indicators are in center, hover center to reveal them, and omarchy bar defaults restores the documented bar, although the migration moves them right on existing Apple users. Document the unit, 0=derive, relevant panel/screen scope and reset behavior alongside size-horizontal/vertical and update the manual if the global migration is retained.
leads.triage: docs part in Opus F9; manual part verified by coordinator (manual/05-the-top-bar.md line 75); published in smaller notes

leads.summary: Transparent-bar contrast helper samples the old bar height after the notch floor enlarges it
leads.consequence: When transparent=true the Process still calls omarchy-bar-text-color with String(root.barSize), which is 26 at stock font size, while this PR renders a 32px or taller top panel. The helper crops the wallpaper using that argument, not the per-screen effective panel thickness, and reads the first Hyprland monitor rather than the actual panel. On a nonuniform wallpaper it may choose text colors against the wrong strip, and changing only notch-height does not trigger this color refresh. Pass effective per-screen thickness when sampling and re-evaluate on floor changes.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified Bar.qml passes root.barSize to omarchy-bar-text-color; published then dropped after self-check noted the mismatch predates the PR

limits: No Apple Silicon hardware or compositor allocated. Visual layering and notch measurements were established only by QML and upstream kernel/Quickshell source, not live display capture.

Windows VM mount-boundary tests use absolute /home targets and umount; review.py did not assert those targets private, so the mount tests were not executed. Static chmod semantics are checked in GNU gnulib source and the repository's test text.

The fetched Quickshell source is upstream master, not an independently pinned installed package release. Exact package-version-specific differences in native margin/exclusion handling remain untested; conclusions about source comparisons are conditional on that version.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** at integer scales the notch math gives the expected floors, and `bar-notch-test.sh` is a real regression test (all 20 assertions pass on this head; on the merge-base it fails at the first one with `bar.notchHeight is not a function`). `notchHeight` results from a direct run of `BarModel.js`:

| Panel (logical size, Qt ratio) | Floor |
|---|---|
| MacBook Pro 14" or 16" at scale 2 | 32 (the 64-row table entry) |
| MacBook Pro 14" or 16" at scale 1 | 64 |
| MacBook Air 13.6" at scale 2 | 32 (full strip, no table entry) |
| Notch hidden (Asahi default `show_notch=0`, 16:10 mode), M1 Air | 0 |
| External `DP-1`, 90° rotated panel | 0 |

The floor reaches the reserved area: with `ExclusionMode.Auto`, Quickshell sets the exclusive zone from `implicitHeight`. Each bar computes its floor from its own screen.

The review found an overlap with open PR #13362, a migration that reaches much further than notched top bars, a hidden-bar regression, an override that ignores the panel checks, and an unrelated Windows VM commit.

### Overlap with open PR #13362

#13362 ("Converge omarchy-mac and omarchy-mx-mac into upstream Omarchy") also implements the camera-notch floor (section 9 of its description). Both PRs add `bin/omarchy-hw-apple-silicon` and `test/shell.d/bar-notch-test.sh` with different contents, and both edit the same regions of `Bar.qml` (after `barSize`, and the margins/`implicitHeight` block) and `BarModel.js`. #13362's version already covers several points below: it parks a hidden bar by its full thickness, applies the calibration only on a panel with a cutout, reads the physical mode from `Hyprland.monitorFor(screen)`, which also works at fractional scales, and draws the center section beside the right one at render time instead of migrating user config.

**Impact:** the two PRs conflict as add/add on two files and textually in `Bar.qml` and `BarModel.js`, and would ship two different Apple Silicon detectors.

**Suggested change:** reconcile with #13362 so only one implementation lands. At minimum, avoid adding a second, different `omarchy-hw-apple-silicon`.

### The migration rewrites more layouts than notched top bars, and misses new installs

`migrations/1789123456.sh` checks only `omarchy-hw-apple-silicon` (`grep -qi apple /proc/device-tree/compatible`), then moves every center widget to the right.

```text
gate: any Apple Silicon device tree
  ├─ notched Pro/Air with notch visible (show_notch=1)  -> intended case
  ├─ notched Pro/Air on Asahi's default show_notch=0   -> rewritten, floor is 0 (panel is 16:10)
  ├─ Mac mini, M1 Air, M1/M2 13" Pro                    -> rewritten, no notch
  └─ bottom or side bar                                 -> rewritten, never under the camera
```

In an isolated run, `bottom-bar` and `left-bar` fixtures were rewritten as well. Whatever the user placed in the center is moved, while earlier bar migrations make narrow edits and avoid overriding a curated bar (for example `1785344985`, "Respect a bar the user already curated"). Moving `omarchy.indicators` also separates its hover peek from the widget: with nothing active (and `alwaysShow` unset, the default) the widget is 0 px wide in the right section, and only hovering the now-empty middle of the bar (around the camera) reveals the inactive icons, next to the tray.

In the other direction, `omarchy-provision-user --first-install` marks every shipped migration as done (`bin/omarchy-provision-user` lines 122-127), and the shipped `config/omarchy/shell.json` still anchors `omarchy.clock` in the center. An Apple Silicon install finalized with `--first-install` therefore keeps the clock under the camera, and `omarchy bar defaults` brings the centered layout back after the migration ran. #13058's second expectation (a default layout that keeps the center clear) is therefore not met.

**Impact:** a one-time, user-visible layout change on machines that have no visible notch or no top bar, and no change for new installs or after `omarchy bar defaults`, which the issue's request for a notch-friendly default layout would cover.

**Suggested change:** gate on a visible notch (for example the eDP mode's aspect ratio or `appledrm`'s `show_notch`) and on a top bar, or move the center aside at render time as #13362 does, so new installs and `omarchy bar defaults` are covered too.

**Migration conventions:** the file is mode 755 where `agents/skills/migrations.md` asks for 0644, it does not start with an `echo` like every other quattro migration, and the hand-picked `1789123456` sorts before 13 migrations already on quattro (`omarchy-dev-add-migration` derives the timestamp from the commit time). It also has no `|| rm -f "$tmp"`, so a `jq` failure (for example `center` stored as a string) leaves a temp file behind.

### A hidden bar leaves a strip on notched panels

The hidden-bar margin still parks the bar by `-root.barSize` (`Bar.qml` 1260-1265), but the surface is now `Math.max(root.barSize, notchFloor)` tall.

| Setup | Floor | Strip left on screen after hiding the bar |
|---|---|---|
| Default `size-horizontal` 26, scale 2 | 32 | 6 px |
| MacBook Air at 1.6 | 40 | 14 px |
| MacBook Pro 14" at 1.333 | 56 | 30 px |

Notification toasts also still clear only `shell.bar.barSize + Style.gapsOut` (`shell/plugins/notifications/Service.qml` 50-52), so with the default gaps they overlap a floored bar by 1 px at a 32 px floor and more at larger floors.

**Impact:** hiding the bar on a notched panel leaves part of it visible, cutting through the widgets at larger floors. These figures come from the source arithmetic and were not observed on a compositor.

**Suggested change:** park and offset by the window's real height (`barWindow.implicitHeight`) rather than `barSize`. `test/shell.d/bar-test.sh` lines 59-63 pin the `-root.barSize` text and need updating with it.

### `[bar] notch-height` applies to every top bar on the machine

`notchFloor` returns `Style.bar.notchHeight` whenever the host is Apple Silicon and the bar is at the top. The `eDP` and aspect-ratio checks only run inside `BarModel.notchHeight`, which the override skips.

**Impact:** a calibrated value also floors top bars on external monitors and on notch-hidden or non-notched panels.

**Suggested change:** apply the override only when the derived value for that screen is above 0. Written with a helper property, that variant still passes the PR's test; the test's regex rejects an inline version.

### Fractional scales never use the measured table

`screen.devicePixelRatio` is Qt's integer `wl_output` scale, and Hyprland sends `ceil(scale)`, so at fractional scales the reconstructed physical size does not match the table and `notchHeight` falls back to the full strip. Hyprland also snaps a requested 1.6 on the 14" panel to 1.333 (logical 2268x1473, ratio 2), giving a 56 px floor instead of the 48 px the table implies. The test case "MacBook Pro 14" at scale 1.6 uses its measured cutout" (1890x1227, ratio 1.6) is a combination Hyprland and Qt do not produce.

**Impact:** at fractional scales the bar is taller than the measured cutout, never shorter.

**Suggested change:** read the physical size and real scale from `Hyprland.monitorFor(screen)`, and base the fractional test case on values Hyprland produces.

### Unrelated Windows VM commit

Commit `2b4b0eba` ("Clear setgid when hardening Windows VM mount folders (#1)") changes `bin/omarchy-windows-vm` and three tests. The PR description does not mention it, and it is also the first commit of #13480, #13477 and #13473. Dedicated PRs for the same setgid problem are also open (#13154, #13213, #12323).

**Verified:** the change itself is correct and needed. GNU chmod keeps an existing directory setgid bit for a 4-digit mode (`chmod 0700` on a 2777 directory gives 2700, `chmod 00700` gives 700), and dockur/windows sets an empty share to 2777, which then fails the exact-700 check on every relaunch. `windows-vm-test.sh` and `windows-vm-compose-test.sh` pass on this head and fail at the new assertions with the base script.

**Impact:** the same unrelated change travels in four open PRs alongside the dedicated ones, so whichever lands first leaves the others to conflict or carry a duplicate.

**Suggested change:** drop the commit here and land the fix once, through one PR.

**Optional test improvement:** the `Bar.qml` and `Style.qml` checks in `bar-notch-test.sh` are regexes over source text. Diagnostic mutants that remove `notch-height` from the `shell.toml` parser (making the override dead) or break the Apple probe command still pass, and so does removing the migration's Apple gate. Evaluating `Style.qml`'s parser on a sample `shell.toml` would catch the first, and running the migration with a non-Apple stub would catch the third.

**Smaller notes:**
- `[bar] notch-height` is not documented next to `size-horizontal` in `docs/omarchy-shell.md`, and `manual/05-the-top-bar.md` still describes the indicators, clock and weather as the center cluster.
- `Bar.qml` repeats the helper's `grep` instead of calling `omarchy-hw-apple-silicon`, so the two can drift. `grep -qi apple` is a substring match.
- The comment calls both table entries "measured on real hardware". The commit that added the 16" entry in omacom/omarchy-mac describes it as inferred from the 14".

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the head, merge-base and current `quattro`, plus Quickshell 0.3.1, Qt 6.11.2 Wayland, Hyprland 0.56.2, the Asahi `appledrm` driver and device trees, the omarchy-mac sources and the fork commits cited in #13058, GNU chmod and dockur/windows. `BarModel.js`, `bar-notch-test.sh`, `bar-test.sh`, `windows-vm-test.sh`, `windows-vm-compose-test.sh`, the migration (on synthetic `shell.json` fixtures with a stubbed Apple Silicon helper) and diagnostic mutants were run in an isolated sandbox. No compositor, QML runtime or Apple hardware was available, so the hidden-bar strip, toast overlap and fractional-scale floors come from source arithmetic, and the 64-row cutout depths are not confirmed on hardware. `windows-vm-mount-boundary-test.sh` could not run in the sandbox.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
